The core operator governing hypnotic suggestion is the sensory hallucination operator H(t), which maps suggestive stimuli S onto perceptual states B. This induces a belief-update process where B evolves according to P(S|B). Emotional hyper-exoitability E(t) emerges as a derivative of this belief modulation, manifesting in heightened motoric expression M. Role-playing transformations R(t) represent a higher-order extension of this belief system, wherein identity becomes a latent variable that shifts under prompt P. These primitives form a closed-loop system where sensory input drives belief change, which in turn influences emotional and behavioral outputs. Failure modes arise when the system lacks sufficient coherence—such as when B is too stable or when P is insufficiently compelling. The epistemic structure reveals a dualism between internal belief and external perception, with suggestion acting as a perturbation to both. The system's stability depends on the balance between top-down expectation and bottom-up sensory fidelity.
